{"content": "Below is a concise guide on how to create a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that is equipped with an **NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU** and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> **Important**: Google Cloud does not use the term *EC2* – that is Amazon Web Services. In Google Cloud the equivalent service is called **Compute Engine**.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| Item | What you need | Why |
|------|---------------|-----|
| Project ID | The ID of the GCP project where you want to create the VM | Needed to target the right project |
| Zone | e.g. `us-central1-a` | GPUs are zone‑specific |
| Quota | Ensure you have GPU quota for the zone | You cannot create a GPU instance if you exceed quota |
| APIs enabled | `Compute Engine API` and `Compute Engine GPU API` | Required for GPU support |

You can enable the APIs via the Cloud Console or by running:

```bash
gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com compute.googleapis.com
```

---

## 2. Using the `gcloud` CLI

The easiest way to spin up a GPU instance is with the `gcloud` command line tool.

```bash
# Replace PROJECT_ID, ZONE, and MACHINE_TYPE with your values
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"   # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

gcloud compute instances create "rtx-a6000-ubuntu" \
  --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
  --zone=${ZONE} \
  --machine-type=${MACHINE_TYPE} \
  --image-family=${IMAGE_FAMILY} \
  --image-project=${IMAGE_PROJECT} \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --accelerator=type=${GPU_TYPE},count=${GPU_COUNT} \
  --maintenance-policy=TERMINATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### Explanation of key flags

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & memory configuration |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk |
| `--accelerator` | Attach the RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--maintenance-policy=TERMINATE` | The VM will be terminated (not stopped) during maintenance events – typical for GPU workloads |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restart if the VM crashes |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: run a script on first boot |
| `--tags` | Allow HTTP/HTTPS traffic |
| `--scopes` | Grant full Cloud Platform access |

> **Tip**: If you want a *preemptible* GPU instance (cheaper but may be reclaimed), add `--preemptible`.

---

## 3. Using the REST API

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine REST API directly, here is a minimal example.

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}

{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {"type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT"}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {"key": "startup-script", "value": "#!/bin/bash\necho Hello World"}
    ]
  }
}
```

### Steps to use the REST API

1. **Obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token** with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.
2. Replace `{PROJECT_ID}`, `{ZONE}`, and `{ACCESS_TOKEN}` with your actual values.
3. Send the request using `curl`, Postman, or any HTTP client.

---

## 4. Quick Checklist

- [ ] Verify GPU quota for the chosen zone.
- [ ] Enable Compute Engine and GPU APIs.
- [ ] Choose a machine type that supports the RTX A6000 (e.g., `n1-standard-8`).
- [ ] Decide whether you want a preemptible instance.
- [ ] Optionally add a startup script to install drivers or CUDA.

---

## 5. Common Pitfalls

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| *Quota exceeded* | Request a quota increase via the Cloud Console or reduce GPU count. |
| *GPU not available in zone* | Switch to a zone that offers the RTX A6000 (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`). |
| *Instance fails to start* | Check the serial console logs for driver errors; ensure you have the correct NVIDIA driver installed. |

---

## 6. Next Steps

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh "rtx-a6000-ubuntu" --project=${PROJECT_ID} --zone=${ZONE}
```

From there, install the NVIDIA driver and CUDA toolkit if you plan to run GPU workloads.

---

**Happy GPU computing!**", "filename": "create-rtx-a6000-instance.md"}
